# Indicators Summary {.unnumbered}


## About These Summaries

These summaries present key regional indicators for the West of England West of England's priority areas. The indicators measure progress against the [West of England Growth Strategy](https://www.westofengland-ca.gov.uk/about-us/our-strategy/west-of-england-growth-plan/). They are not intended to directly measure outcomes or outputs for WECA projects, but rather to provide a high-level overview of regional trends and performance. A wide range of factors affect these indicators, including residents’ and businesses’ actions, long-term trends, national and international economic conditions, as well as regional interventions.

The default geography includes North Somerset as part of a wider West of England region unless otherwise stated. A process is underway to incorporate North Somerset into the West of England Combined Authority.

## Priority Areas

- Contributing to national [economic growth](/chapters/01-economy/) helping our businesses succeed and creating jobs
- Connecting the region through [public transport & active travel](/chapters/02-transport/)
- Building [affordable and attractive homes in sustainable communities](/chapters/03-place/)
- Empowering residents with the [skills](/chapters/04-skills/) to access the jobs that will shape our future
- Making the West of England the home for [green jobs and green growth](/chapters/05-environment/)
- [Lifting children and families out of poverty](/chapters/06-child-poverty/) in the West of England

```{r}
#| label: overall_summary
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
source(here::here("scripts", "R", "_common.R"))
rv <- build_reporting_view(collate_fact())
format_overall_summary(
  rv,
  core_dim_data_tbl,
  title = "West of England Regional Priorities",
  subtitle = "Latest published value per indicator"
)
```

## How to Use These Summaries

- Use the **sidebar navigation** to jump to any chapter
- Each summary is self-contained and can be read independently
- The majority of time series data are for a calendar year, but some data represent different time periods, for example academic years. Where data are update more frequently than yearly they are provided at this cadence.

## Data Sources

Indicators draw on a range of national and local data sources. Each chapter documents its specific sources within the analysis. Data refresh schedules are noted where applicable.
